long_biography.plain_text:
Roland Dickey Sr. grew up around the hickory pits of the original Dickey’s Barbecue Pit in Dallas, learning recipes and restaurant work from his parents. He was completing his senior year at Southern Methodist University and planning law school when his father died in 1967. Dickey and his brother, T.D., stepped in to help their mother and stayed to build the business.

The brothers turned one barbecue stand into several restaurants, added catering and began franchising in 1994. Dickey helped shape menu recipes and the operating traditions behind the chain, while his first franchise partner grew into a multi-unit operator. He later transferred day-to-day leadership to his son but continued as chairman, cookbook author, franchisee visitor and public face of the family brand.
